To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic moderate ethanol feeding to male rats resulted in increased hepatic synthesis and secretion of apo E of VLDL and HDL, and increased hepatic secretion of apo A-I.
the heavy ethanol diet resulted in a 52% increase in liver protein synthesis, and 2.75 fold increase in liver total lipid synthesis, with no significant change in liver DNA content.
chronic moderate or heavy alcohol consumption results in a significant increase of liver weight, liver protein, liver lipids, plasma lipids, plasma apoproteins, and liver apoproteins.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the influence of ethanol on the synthesis and secretion of apoproteihs of HDL and VLDL by the perfused rat liver.
the effects of ethanol on lipids and lipoproten metabolism.
the effects of chronic ethanol ingestion in rats on the metabolism of lipids and apoproteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ethanol feeding to rats resulted in an increase in liver mass, liver lipids, plasma lipids and lipogenic enzymes.
the chronic heavy ethanol consumption resulted in an increase in liver weight, protein and lipid synthesis, and plasma lipids.
chronic heavy and moderate ethanol consumption results in significant changes in lipoprotein metabolism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic heavy ethanol consumption in the rat resulted in increased hepatic lipids and lipids in the plasma and increased hepatic VLDL and HDL synthesis and secretion.
ethanol feeding resulted in an increased synthesis of VLDL apo E and decreased apo E in HDL.
chronic heavy ethanol feeding resulted not only in the inhibition of hepatic lipoprotein secretion but also in the inhibition of the synthesis of the apoprotein moiety of VLDL and HDL.
The main takeaway from our work is that

chronic ethanol feeding results in a significant decrease in the secretion of apo E from the liver, which is associated with the increased secretion of apo E in the VLDL and decreased secretion in HDL.
the liver is not the only organ involved in alcohol metabolism.
heavy ethanol feeding to rats resulted in increased liver weight and total lipids with no significant changes in liver DNA content.
